questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Relevant Master courses at uni, and a city full of culture and life

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. It was possible to get help via e-mail with pretty fast responses, or you could go to the international office

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a welcome seminar at the university, with presentations from the Erasmus coordinators and the students responsible for events etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I was not super easy, but it depends on what you are looking for. I wanted to live with my friend, and finding an appropriate and not too expensive apartment for two was difficult. We used Idealista, but you need to invest some time, since the good apartments went fast
If you are looking for a room in a shared apartment with other Erasmus students, Facebook is your friends, a lot of people found housing there.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be aware of scammers on the housing websites - they can make a contract look very real. In Barcelona it is normal to pay a deposit just to reserve the apartment before signing a contract, so some people uses this to take money for apartments that aren't real. Always check that the apartment actually exist and is available for rent through the claimed housing company

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The suggested page by the university only had a few options when we tried it two months before arrival

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Course changes was expected and handled easily

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: At the presentation seminar you received a paper with your pre-approved courses, and then you had some weeks to attend (check out) the courses and make sure that the time table was good, and then you could go to the international office and be registrated to the courses

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could make appointments at the IO or write an email. The teachers were also happy to help and suggest other courses or send you the material until the registration went through

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress if you have to change some courses, they are used to it

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: A little different levels in the different courses. A lot of them were only 3 ETCS, and therefore quite short - It seemed to me that the expectations did not always match the number of credits.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Not too different. In Barcelona they also liked to involve the students with questions and discussion

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee, beer, wine etc. was much cheaper than in Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Erasmus Barcelona offers a lot of activities, there are things to do every day if you want to. Beer pong tournaments and free entry to clubs are a hit, but also museum trips, beach volley and trips to nearby attractions and other cities are available

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The welcome dinner in the first week, and generally many of the activities in the two welcome weeks, to meet people. Volley is also a great way to talk to new people

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Montserrat is beautiful for a hike. The city Sitges near Barcelona is great for a beach day - charming and less busy

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The people are very kind, which makes it easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really, just be open and not afraid to ask for help, that is an easy way to start a conversation - fx if they can show you the library

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The structure of the lessons meant there there were no breaks during class, and rarely people stuck around to wait for another class. This made it difficult to make contact, since everybody went out after class

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The tempo. They talk fast, but they are not in a rush otherwise. In the cafes, the supermarket etc. everything is more slow and relaxed.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It is likely that not all your courses are very relevant (if they are 3 ECTS you'll need a lot of different courses), and it is okay to lose motivation sometimes. If you should fail something, it is not the end of the world.
Remember that you are on exchange for more that academic purposes - get out and experience something - it doesn't have to be something big, it can just be a walk in the neighborhood or finding a new icecream place to try.
It is normal to miss home even though you are having the time of your life

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improved language skills and many cultural experiences - food in particular

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Some courses requiered some former knowledge that I didn't have, since I only took the second semester on the Master - this made it a bit difficult to follow sometimes

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to ask the teachers for help

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
